senses.definition: A senior official in a college or university, who may be in charge of a division or faculty (for example, the dean of science) or have some other advisory or disciplinary function (for example, the dean of students).

quotes.text:
Lucretius versus the Lake Poets ' Nature I loved ; and next to Nature , Art . '
Dean , adult education may seem silly .
What of it though ? I got some willy - nilly
The other evening at your college deanery .
And grateful for it ( Let's not be facetious!)[…]
quotes.reference: 1995 October 25, Robert Frost, Richard Poirier, Robert Frost: Collected Poems, Prose, & Plays (LOA #81) (DE-601)374069697: Library of America series), Library of America, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 357:

senses.definition: A dignitary or presiding officer in certain church bodies, especially an ecclesiastical dignitary, subordinate to a bishop, in charge of a chapter of canons.
The senior member of some group of people.
examples: dean of the diplomatic corps - a country's most senior ambassador
dean of the House - the longest-serving member of a legislature

senses.definition: (intransitive, rare) To serve as a dean.
(transitive, Oxbridge, otherwise rare, informal) To send (a student) to see the dean of a college or university.
(Sussex, chiefly in place names) A hill.
(Northumbria, chiefly in place names) Alternative form of dene.
